questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of waterloo is well known for its strong Computer Science department, being the best in Canada and I also wanted to live in Canada.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Getting from Toronto airport to waterloo can be done by bus, and then in waterloo you can get a uber or a bus to your accommodation on the day of your arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some tours showing the university and the different buildings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding housing was rather difficult. The uni halls were mostly for first year students and it's difficult to find a short term lease for a flat in a city you cannot visit before you stay. So I ended up going with Airbnb because its more flexible but my location was not optimal. Overall the housing was okay. There are many scams for housing, especially on facebook groups so I recommend to not sign any sublease of any apartment you have not seen in person.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in Laurelwood which is 15 min with the bus from the uni. It was a quiet area but there was nothing going on because it was very residential and you would need a car for a lot of things. You need to decide if you want to live somewhere more central like downtown Kitchener or uptown waterloo which might be more busy and could be a worse flat for the price or rather a bit further away and a quiet place. Try to get some flatmates, my roommate was also a uwaterloo student and that definitely helped.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have liked special housing for exchange students such as the KU housing foundation does.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Courses are on a first come first serve basis, I recommend you register for many classes when it opens, and then in the first week you go to these classes and you can drop classes you don't linke the first weeks and register for other ones in the first week.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a website called quest.uwaterloo where you can select the classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much really, on the course website you can find classes you are eligible for.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are a Master student for example I chose 2 computer science classes (my major) and then I chose a non-CS class. I recommend that you try a new class on something that interests you and has a bit lower workload as your exchange is not only about academia. A language class can be fun for example.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It's a very fast paced environment where you will have many assignments and a research project in most classes. You need to do some reading and definitely spend a lot of time on the assignments as they are supposed to be rather difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was similar, you have a good relationship to the teachers but most of the tutorials were online which could still be because of covid.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Data-Intensive Distributed Computing
- Introduction to AI
- Italian language class

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend my three classes, I enjoyed the combination of AI, Big data and a complete different class on a language a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Mobile phone bills are expensive in Canada. The food is also expensive because of high Tax and Tip

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was free for students which is great

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Amazing sports facilities (Many basket ball courts, Badminton, martial arts, full ice ring for hockey, full indoor soccer field, 2 gyms). In addition, you can watch the university teams play against other unis on weekends.
There were also many events on campus to take part. You have many food options on campus such as kebab, subway, starbucks inside the buildings.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend joining an intramural, which is a sports league where you compete against other students on a weekly basis. I did it with squash and met many people and had lots of good games.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend visiting Toronto (2h bus), Montreal (6h train or 1.5h flight), New York (1.5h Flight) and Mexico (4h flight to Cancun).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the culture is not different from europe

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in sports, go to events in the first weeks and sit next to other students in class to meet new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There are not as many partys as for example in Denmark. Alcohol can only be bought in liquor stores. But there are no student bars from the uni and generally on campus there is never alcohol. This is not a problem but it was interesting to see the difference.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are generally very friendly and helpful, it was always easy to ask for help when needed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) The sports facility is amazing, make sure to pick some new sports to learn. I started squash and muay thai for example
2) You need to work to pass the classes, this is a rather competitive uni and I had a similar workload to my masters in ucph.
3) Travel around! The grade conversion is Pass / Fail which means you should not aim for 100 and spend all day studying

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend to book a trip over reading week, and also to score high points on the first assignments so that you can have less to study in december and travel around.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Visiting new places and making friends with locals.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing traveling and keeping up with classes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
